Download prepared mortality rates from the HMD

Source: R/get_database_rates.R
get_mortality_hmd.Rd

Download mortality rate schedules from the Human Mortality Database in the format that mortality() expects. Requires user name and password and the HMDHFDplus package.

Usage

get_mortality_hmd(
  country,
  year,
  username = Sys.getenv("HMD_USERNAME"),
  password = Sys.getenv("HMD_PASSWORD"),
  shape = "1x1",
  open_age = NULL
)

Arguments

country

A single HMD population code, such as "USA".

year

One whole-number calendar year or a nonempty vector of distinct years. For grouped HMD periods, supply their starting years. All requested years must exist in the product.

username

Database username. Defaults to the HMD_USERNAME environment variable.

password

Database password. Defaults to the HMD_PASSWORD environment variable.

shape

Native HMD age-by-period shape: "1x1" (default), "1x5", "1x10", "5x1", "5x5", or "5x10".

open_age

Optional nonnegative whole age at a native age-band start. Default NULL keeps the source age layout. Otherwise retain rates below this age and pool Deaths_<shape> and Exposures_<shape> into one [open_age, Inf) rate for each sex and source period.

Value

A validated mortality rate tibble with a source attribute recording years, shape and represented source periods. Multiple-year requests include time_start/time_end. With open_age, source metadata also records the pooling method, products and tail totals.

Details

To use this function, users will need to install the HMDHFDplus package with:

install.packages("HMDHFDplus")

Users will also need to either pass a user name and password to the function arguments or set the these values in the .Renviron as follows:

HMD_USERNAME="username here"
HMD_PASSWORD="password here"

A single requested year returns a static schedule without calendar columns. Multiple years return time_start/time_end for the selected source periods, in chronological order.

HMD rate schedules include an open-ended category at age 110+, but with many historical sources this will lead to missing values at some earlier ages. Users can avoid this by using the optional open_age argument to specify an open-ended age. The function will pool source death and exposure at this open age band from HMD to construct the open-age death rate.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
mort_rates_usa <- get_mortality_hmd("USA", year = 2000)
mort_rates_swe <- get_mortality_hmd("SWE", year = 1891:2000, open_age = 95)
} # }
